<!-- pr-reviewer: 8426dc0be03a469fdbc70bf61f71a32291590897 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.**

### What looks good
- Each of the five posts (`fanuc.cps`, `mazak.cps`, `doosan-dnm.cps`, `grblhal.cps`, `tormach.cps`) adds the dwell to the cycle signature only for the cycles that read P: G82 and G89, and also G86 on grblHAL and Tormach. G73, G83, G84 and G85 do not read P, so a dwell change there does not split a group.
- A changed dwell goes through the existing "signature changed" branch: `G80`, then the retract word (`G99` on the Fanuc family and Tormach; `G98` stays modal on grblHAL, and `G80` does not change group 10), then a full cycle block with its own P. No new retract path is added and no retract is lost.
- BACKBORE at dwell 0 posts G85. `CycleKind::BackBore` is defined as "feed in AND feed out" (`crates/cl/src/cl/cycle.rs:31`). G85 is feed in, feed out at F, no dwell, on Fanuc, Mazak EIA, Doosan (Fanuc 0i) and LinuxCNC/PathPilot/grblHAL. G89 is the same motion with a dwell at the bottom. Thus the tool motion and the retract do not change. On `origin/main`, a BACKBORE at dwell 0 was G89 with no P (the P word was written only for `ms > 0`). That output ran a stale modal P, or a LinuxCNC-family control refused it after G80. The swap removes that defect.
- REAM was already G85, so G85 is a cycle that these posts already write. No golden file has G85 or G89, so no golden changes. Programs with one dwell keep the short form (`same_dwell_keeps_the_open_group`).
- The G83 dwell refusals stay before the signature code and do not change: PR #2048 (Fanuc family, `p.P > 0`) and PR #2351 (grblHAL, Tormach). `g83_dwell` and `g83_dwell_linuxcnc` pass.
- No `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic` in post code. The test file has a provenance line and a Gate map, and it is in the lowest crate (`camcraft-post`). The decision file is present. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #2360`. No process file is changed.

### Results (locally, PR head; the head already contains `origin/main`, so the trial merge is "Already up to date")
| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` | 80 binaries, 674 passed, 0 failed |
| `camcraft-app` `conformance` | 7 passed |
| `recorded_post_streams` | 5 passed |
| `grblhal_post` | 9 passed |
| `doosan_dnm_a_state` | 2 passed |
| `tormach_post`, `tormach_end_units`, `tormach_fourth_axis`, `tormach_machines`, `tormach_program_end`, `tormach_routers`, `tormach_safe_retract`, `tormach_toolchange_lift` | 10, 8, 12, 6, 3, 5, 4, 3 passed |
| `dwell_cycles_modal_p` on the five post files of `origin/main` | 4 failed, 1 passed (`same_dwell_keeps_the_open_group`), as the PR says |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

CR-byte check: 0 CR bytes in each changed file, the same as on `origin/main`.

### Requested before merge
None.

### Notes (not blocking)
1. No test has a tool change between two dwell holes. Each post sets `inCycle = false` at a tool change, so the next hole writes a full block with its own P. The existing code covers this and the PR does not change it.
2. A zero-dwell G86 on grblHAL and Tormach still posts without P. A LinuxCNC-family control refuses that block after G80. This is visible, not silent, and it is tracked in #2362.
3. Haas writes `G89 P0` (#2350), and these five posts write G85. The decision file records the reason: `P0` is documented for Haas only.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
